name: Brigade

overview_markdown:
Brigade positions itself as an enterprise-grade personal intelligence ecosystem rather than a single app. Its core differentiator is frictionless authentication: instead of juggling API keys, users sign in with existing Claude, ChatGPT, or Copilot subscriptions, or reuse active Claude Code / Codex CLI sessions. API keys remain on the local machine with no telemetry and no middleman proxying.

The headline feature is B³ (Brigade Bloody Benchmark), introduced in v1.9.0, which exposes your agent crew to the open internet through HTTPS tunnels (Cloudflare by default, or self-hosted bore/frp/sish relays) with an invisible secret key gating access. The philosophy is that the only benchmark that matters is real strangers probing your agents at 3 a.m. Recent releases (v1.38–1.39) added a durable team collaboration mode and hardened runtime message pagination, showing active, disciplined engineering with release-please automation and PR-gated main branch.

Compared to OpenClaw, Brigade trades ecosystem breadth for auth simplicity and adversarial testing tooling. OpenClaw offers thousands of community skills and broad messaging-channel coverage, while Brigade focuses on a polished CLI experience, subscription reuse, and real-world exposure benchmarking. Its TypeScript stack means moderate resource footprint, and its tunnel-exposure features, while gated, warrant careful operational review.
